MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the best form is the most upright creation, the return to the lowest is decrepit old age, and the reward of the faithful is undiminished.

MUJAHID:v2p770/r4.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p770/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p770/r4.claim: Mujahid says the best form is the best creation.

MUQATIL:95:1-6/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:95:1-6/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:95:1-6/r2.claim: The best human form is upright walking on two legs rather than four, especially the beauty and strength of youth.

FARRA:v3p276/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p276/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p276/r6.claim: The best human form is bodily balance and the vigor of youth; God then returns many people to decrepit old age, though the wording is singular and distributive.

FARRA:v3p276/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p276/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p276/r7.claim: A singular expression can refer to only a portion of a person's wealth, as in the verse describing Abū Bakr's giving.

MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r2.claim: Aḥsani taqwīm means the best form or image.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p382#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p382#2/r1.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p382#2/r1.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi explain the best stature as the best form.

TUSTARI:95:4/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:95:4/r1.claim: The best form means the finest stature and appearance.

TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r1.claim: The declaration that humanity was created in the best constitution answers the opening oath, ‘By the fig and the olive.’

TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r2.claim: Qatadah says the oath lands on the statement that God created humanity in the best constitution.

TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the best constitution as the most balanced creation.

TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim explains the phrase as humanity being made in the best image or form.

TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says the verse describes the best image.

TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as the best image and, in another report, the best creation.

TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r7.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r7.claim: Qatadah and al-Kalbi both interpret the phrase as the best image.

TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r8.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p510#2/r8.claim: Another interpretation takes the verse to mean that humans reach their prime in youth, healthy skin, and strength, when they are most balanced and upright.

TAB-FULL:v24p512/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p512/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p512/r1.claim: Ikrima describes the best constitution as the strong, firm-skinned young person.

TAB-FULL:v24p512/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p512/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p512/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the phrase refers to a person's youth at the beginning of growth.

TAB-FULL:v24p512/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p512/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p512/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas explains the excellence of human form by saying other creatures are bent forward, unlike humans.

TAB-FULL:v24p512/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p512/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p512/r4.claim: The strongest reading is that humans were created in the most beautiful and balanced form; ‘best constitution’ modifies an omitted noun, as if it said ‘in a constitution of the best constitution.’

ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r4.claim: The human was created in the best form.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies the fig and olive as edible fruit, Sinai as the blessed Mount, and Mecca as the secure city; he reads best form as finest shape, the lowest state as Hell, and the believers' reward as uncounted.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says people are returned to senility until their minds fail.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r2.claim: Ikrimah glosses the best form as youth and strength.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says the best form is the finest appearance, while the lowest state is the Fire in the worst appearance.

NAHHAS:v5p256/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p256/r3.claim: He says every creature was created bent over except the human being.

NAHHAS:v5p256/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r4.speaker: عكرمة
NAHHAS:v5p256/r4.claim: He interprets the best stature as youth, strength, and vigor.

NAHHAS:v5p256/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r5.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p256/r5.claim: With al-Nakhaʿī, he interprets the best stature as the finest form.

NAHHAS:v5p256/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p256/r6.claim: The finest form is the best account: taqwīm is ‘a most excellent proportion,’ with the adjective standing for the described noun.

SULAMI:v2p406#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r1.claim: The best proportion means the most beautiful form.

SULAMI:v2p406#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r2.claim: The best proportion means the best exemplar.

SULAMI:v2p406#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r3.claim: The best proportion means complete gnosis.

SULAMI:v2p406#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r4.claim: The best proportion is the perfection of the inner secret as thoughts arise.

SULAMI:v2p406#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r5.claim: Perfect proportion is an attribute established in God that worship cannot fully express or exhaust in words.

SULAMI:v2p406#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p406#3/r6.claim: The human is adorned with intellect, supported by command, guided by discernment, tall in stature, and takes food by hand.

THALABI:v10p239/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p239/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p239/r14.claim: Humans were created upright and in the best image, unlike other creatures made bent forward on their faces.

THALABI:v10p239/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p239/r15.speaker: أبو بكر بن ظاهر
THALABI:v10p239/r15.claim: He describes human excellence as intellect, instruction by divine command, discernment, tall stature, and the ability to take food by hand.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r16.claim: Mawardi says human may mean people generally, using the singular as a collective, or a particular person described in a way that applies to people.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the particular person as Kaldah ibn Asid.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r18.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r18.claim: Muqatil identifies the person as Abu Jahl.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r19.claim: A further identification says the person is the Messenger of God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r20.claim: Ibn Abbas says the best form is the most balanced creation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r21.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r21.claim: Abu al-Aliya says it means the best image.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r22.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r22.claim: Ikrima says it means youth and strength.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r23.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r23.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as upright stature, unlike other animals, which are bent over.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r24.claim: Mawardi suggests the best form could mean the fullest intellect, since intellect is what makes a person well formed.

QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r10.claim: This wording establishes that God has no form or bodily configuration: when an attribute is shared with creation, its perfection belongs to God, yet the verse calls the human form the best stature.

QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r9.claim: Humanity was created in the best stature through upright posture and the beautiful arrangement of its limbs.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r1.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r1.claim: The description of the secure city applies grammatically to the place but means its resident and visitor; it is secure under religious law and must not be harmed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r2.claim: The human means Adam and his descendants; the best form is a well-composed and proportioned creation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r3.claim: They gloss the best form as the best image and explain it as proportioning the image according to a fitting composition.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r4.claim: Humans are created upright and tall, unlike other living creatures bent over their faces, and use their hands to take food.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r5.claim: The oath's point is that God blessed humanity with a well-proportioned creation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p151#2/r6.claim: The human reaches the best proportion in uprightness and youthful prime, then is returned to decrepit age.

WAHIDI-QT:95:4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:95:4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:95:4/r1.claim: Humans were created in a well-proportioned form, standing upright and able to take food with their hands.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:95:1-6/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:95:1-6/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:95:1-6/r3.claim: The best form is a balanced upright figure that can take food by hand.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r1.claim: Humanity is created upright and in the finest form; unlike other animals, which lean face-down, a person stands tall, takes food by hand, and is adorned with intellect and discernment.

KASHSHAF:95:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:95:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:95:4/r1.claim: Humanity is created with the best balanced form, shape, and arrangement of limbs.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r11.claim: أحسن تقويم means the most balanced, beautiful bodily form, with well-proportioned and arranged limbs.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p499#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p499#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p499#2/r19.claim: The oath answers to creation of humanity in the best proportion.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p499#2/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p499#2/r20.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p499#2/r20.claim: Some scholars generalize the statement and say the human is the best-proportioned of all creatures.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r1.claim: Some people did not treat as broken a divorce oath that a wife was more beautiful than the sun.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r2.speaker: النخعي ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r2.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi, Mujahid, and Qatada say best proportion means the beauty of the human form and senses.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r3.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r3.claim: Others take it to mean upright stature.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r4.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says the best proportion is intellect, perception, and discernment.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r5.claim: Ikrima says youth and strength, but Ibn Atiyya rejects this because some animals exceed humans in those qualities.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya's preferred view combines the other physical and intellectual senses of excellent human proportion; insan is generic.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r7.claim: The grammar implies fi taqwim ahsani taqwim, since the adjective ahsan must modify an understood noun.

TABRISI:95:1-3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:1-3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:95:1-3/r1.claim: Taqwīm means shaping something into its proper, balanced form.

TABRISI:95:4-6/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TABRISI:95:4-6/r1.claim: Humanity, Adam and his descendants, was created in the finest form; Mujahid and Qatada share this view.

TABRISI:95:4-6/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:95:4-6/r2.claim: The best form means standing upright, unlike other animals that move face-down.

TABRISI:95:4-6/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:95:4-6/r3.claim: The human form is complete and balanced, distinguished by speech, discernment, and planning, and this may allude to youth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r1.claim: The human may be Kulda ibn Asīd.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r2.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r2.claim: Alternatively, the human is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r3.claim: Another reported identification is Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r4.claim: Al-Māwardī cites the alternatives of ʿUtba and Shayba.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r5.claim: Many interpreters, including Muqātil, take al-insān generically to mean humankind.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r6.claim: Aḥsan taqwīm is interpreted as the most balanced creation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r7.claim: Aḥsan taqwīm may mean an upright stature.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p171/r8.claim: Aḥsan taqwīm may mean the best form.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p172/r1.claim: Aḥsan taqwīm may mean youth and strength.

RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r1.claim: Human refers to the human kind; taqwim means shaping and adjusting something into the form it ought to have.

RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r2.claim: One explanation is physical: unlike other creatures, humans stand upright and use their hands to take food.

RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r3.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r3.claim: Al-Aṣamm interprets the best form as complete intellect, understanding, manners, knowledge, and speech, covering inward character as well as outward form.

RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r4.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r4.claim: Yahya ibn Aktham takes the verse as proof of human beauty: a jurist who used the verse to answer a husband's oath said he was not legally in breach for preferring his wife to the moon.

RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p11#2/r5.claim: A pious person's prayer asks that the best outward forms granted in this world be matched by the best deeds in the next, namely forgiveness and pardon.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r1.claim: The oath's answer is that God created the human; here it may mean a disbeliever, identified as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira or Kalda ibn Asid, in connection with deniers of resurrection.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes human as Adam and all his descendants.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r3.speaker: عامة المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r3.claim: Most commentators explain the best constitution as human uprightness and the prime of youth, with reason, articulate speech, grasping hands, and fingers distinguishing humans from creatures bent face-down.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r4.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir describes the best constitution as beautified by intellect, able to obey and discern, tall, and able to take food by hand.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says no creation is more complete than the human, whom God made living, knowing, able, willing, speaking, hearing, seeing, and governing wisely.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi interprets the report that Adam was created in God's image as referring to attributes or meanings, not a bodily likeness; the variant about the Merciful cannot mean a physical form.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r7.claim: A jurist avoids divorce in an oath comparing his wife to the moon by citing this verse: humans are the most beautiful creation, so nothing is more beautiful than the wife.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:95:4-5/r8.claim: The verse indicates human beauty inside and out through its form and assembled faculties; philosophers call the human a microcosm because created things are gathered in it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r2.claim: Humanity was formed in the best proportions: upright, beautiful, and endowed with the properties of beings and counterparts of possibilities.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p347#5/r1.claim: Al-insān means the human species, created with the finest proportions in form and bodily features.

QASHANI:95:4-5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:95:4-5/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:95:4-5/r1.claim: Humanity’s best form harmonizes light and darkness, unites opposites, and mediates between two worlds, yielding balanced temperament, perfect species, and finest creature.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r2.claim: The surah is Meccan for most commentators; Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatada say Madinan.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p502/r3.claim: After praising the Prophet's perfected creation and character, the surah describes the one who opposes him being brought low in this world and the next; mankind was created ready to accept truth but may be moved to a base state.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r7.speaker: النخعي ومجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r7.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī, Mujāhid, and Qatada say the best stature means a beautiful form and senses; other opinions specify uprightness, intellect, or youth and strength.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r8.claim: The author prefers the general sense: mankind was created with every feature that counts as the best; al-insān is a generic noun and a noun is implicit after أحسن.

SAMIN-DURR:95:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:95:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:95:4/r1.claim: ‘Laqad khalaqna’ is the answer to the oath; ‘fi ahsani taqwim’ means ‘in a configuration of the best form’, with an omitted noun understood.

SAMIN-DURR:95:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:95:4/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:95:4/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa takes ‘fi ahsani taqwim’ as a circumstantial of ‘al-insan’, understanding taqwim as constitution rather than the act of shaping, which properly belongs to the Creator.

SAMIN-DURR:95:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:95:4/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:95:4/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa also allows an omitted construct (‘best uprightness of form’) or an extra ‘fi’, yielding ‘we formed him in the best form’; the author says these complications are unnecessary.

IBNKATHIR:95:4/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:95:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:95:4/r1.claim: The oath's subject is that God created humankind in the best form, upright, with proportionate and beautiful limbs.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links this surah to the two preceding ones: human form seems to promise shared perfection, yet people diverge toward ascent or degradation.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r2.claim: Those who rise answer a divine call quickly, while people who resist follow what was written for them; each person is made ready for the end appointed to them.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r3.claim: A fair-minded person should know that everyone is enabled for the end they were created for and should ask God for sincerity; whoever finds good should thank God.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r4.claim: The surah explains the Prophet's abundant favors and signs of divine love: God neither forsook nor disliked him, and bestowed these gifts by grace rather than earned merit.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r5.claim: An excellent human form alone cannot save someone: without divine guidance and prior felicity, a person sees only himself and mistakes that for perfection, ending in the lowest state.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r5.claim: An excellent human form alone cannot save someone: without divine guidance and prior felicity, a person sees only himself and mistakes that for perfection, ending in the lowest state.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#s095/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#s095/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#s095/r3.claim: The surah continues al-Sharḥ by presenting the Prophet’s kind as creation’s finest, Abraham as its noblest root, Mecca as the best land, and God as the one who raises or lowers whom He wills.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468/r3.claim: Linked to al-Sharḥ, the surah presents humanity and especially the Prophet as the finest created kind, Abraham as its noblest root, and Mecca as its best land; God raises or lowers whom He wills.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r1.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r1.claim: Ibn Burjān says humanity is innately formed upon Islam, the upright religion.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r2.claim: Humanity's real distinction is intellect, which can guide it from ruin toward Paradise through faith and righteous action; prophets and their followers exemplify this capacity.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r3.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r3.claim: Al-Baghawī describes the human as tall, able to take food by hand, and endowed with intellect and discernment.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r4.claim: Intellects are broadly comparable, but natural dispositions steer them differently; varied strengths and weaknesses help organize people's trades and social life.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r5.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r5.claim: Al-Qushayrī argues that the verse proves God is exalted above composition and form, since every shared perfection belongs to God in its fullest degree.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r6.claim: The author rejects the maxim that no world could be more excellent than this one: God's possible creations are unlimited, and other worlds could differ in size and excellence.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472#2/r7.claim: Against philosophers who deny divine choice, the author follows Sunni theologians including al-Ashʿarī and al-Ghazālī in affirming God's unlimited power to create any possible world.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r1.claim: Human beings combine reason with appetite and self-absorption, which can make them forget what matters; the angels anticipated conflict and corruption from this combination.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r2.claim: Best form includes spirit and intellect, upright stature, beauty, and a combination of faculties and senses suited to the human purpose.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r3.claim: The verse also describes the original, sound disposition that God prepared to accept truth.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r4.speaker: الأصفهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v8p472/r4.claim: Al-Asfahani likewise interprets the verse through the primordial disposition, paralleling his reading of humanity's original unity.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.claim: The surah's oath recalls the Torah's account of God coming from Sinai, Seir, and Paran; ideal creation, the righteous, and the fallen summarize the Torah's beginnings, laws, and later history.

DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.claim: An explicitly weak report identifies the Fig with Syria and Olive with Palestine, Sinai with Moses' mountain, and the secure town with Mecca; it allegorizes the human as Muhammad, the lowest as idolaters, and the exception as the four caliphs.

DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.claim: He identified the Fig as Noah's mosque on al-Judi, Olive as Jerusalem, Sinai as its mosque, and the secure town as Mecca; return to the lowest means extreme old age, excusing contemporaries whose minds failed and preserving their prior reward.

DURR-FULL:v8p554/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r1.claim: He identified Fig and Olive as the Sacred Mosque and al-Aqsa, where the Night Journey ended; Sinai as Moses' mountain, Mecca as the secure town, upright stature as standing erect, and the lowest as decrepit age.

DURR-FULL:v8p554/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r2.claim: He identified the Fig with Damascus's mountain and Olive with Jerusalem's, Sinai as a blessed wooded mountain and Mecca as the secure town; the oath ends at verse 4, the lowest is Hell, and the final command means be certain of God's proof.

DURR-FULL:v8p554/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r4.claim: He identified the Fig as the Companions of the Cave's mosque, the Olive as Elijah's mosque, Sinai as the Mount's mosque, and the secure town as Mecca.

DURR-FULL:v8p554/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r6.speaker: كعب الأحبار
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r6.claim: He identified the Fig as Damascus, the Olive as Jerusalem, Sinai as where God spoke to Moses, and the secure town as Mecca.

DURR-FULL:v8p554/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r7.speaker: أبو حبيب الحارث بن محمد
DURR-FULL:v8p554/r7.claim: He named four sacred mountains: Zayta/Jerusalem, Sinai, Tina/Damascus, and Tima/Mecca, linking them to the four oaths.

DURR-FULL:v8p555/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r1.speaker: زيد بن ميسرة
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r1.claim: He repeated the sacred-mountain identification and specified Sinai as where God spoke to Moses.

DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.claim: He glossed finest stature as the most balanced form, return as extreme old age, and an unending reward as undiminished.

DURR-FULL:v8p555/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r2.speaker: الحكم
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r2.claim: He identified the Fig with Damascus, Olive with Palestine, and the secure town with Mecca.

DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.claim: He identified the first oaths as fruit, the blessed mountain, and Mecca; human creation is in the finest image, return is to Fire, believers are excepted, and their reward is uncounted.

DURR-FULL:v8p555/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r8.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r8.claim: He reports that the Prophet told Khuzayma ibn Thabit that the secure town is Mecca.

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.claim: When believers reach extreme old age, their earlier good deeds continue to be credited; age neither harms their former reward nor adds sins for later incapacity.

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.claim: He glossed the finest form as the best image and the lowest state as Hell in the worst form.

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.claim: He identified the oaths with actual figs and olives, Sinai as the blessed mountain, and Mecca; finest form is youth and strength, senility is the lowest, and the believer retains reward without reproach.

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r4.claim: He identified the oaths with actual figs and olives, finest form with a beautiful image, and the lowest with Hell.

BURSEVI:v10p360/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360/r1.claim: The body's sensory and limb-based acts derive their honor from the heart, which derives it from spirit and secret; the bodily form is thus worthy of the oath and exposed to satanic whispering.

BURSEVI:v10p360/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360/r2.claim: Taqwim means making something as it ought to be by proportion and adjustment; qama means to stand upright or be sound, and qawwama means to straighten.

BURSEVI:v10p360/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360/r3.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
BURSEVI:v10p360/r3.claim: When a ruler swore his wife was more beautiful than the moon or she would be divorced, all jurists found him in breach except Yahya ibn Aktham, who said he was not, since God calls the human being the best-proportioned creation.

BURSEVI:v10p360/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360/r4.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v10p360/r4.claim: Al-Mufradat reads the best stature as the human distinctions from animals: reason, understanding, and an upright build that indicates mastery over worldly things.

BURSEVI:v10p360/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360/r5.claim: The human being is proportionate in body and endowed inwardly with life, knowledge, will, power, hearing, sight, and speech; these divine-like attributes are the true form, making the human a manifestation of majesty, beauty, and perfection.

BURSEVI:v10p360/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360/r6.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p360/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says God created Adam in His form; the author connects this to the saying that knowing oneself leads to knowing one's Lord.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r1.claim: Al-insān means humanity generally, including believers and unbelievers; the connected exception later supports this broad scope.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r10.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم وبعض الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r10.claim: They ruled that a husband's conditional divorce does not take effect if his wife is not more beautiful than the moon, citing this verse.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r11.claim: Poets often praise a beloved as fairer than the full moon, but the real distinction between human and moon is as clear as morning.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r2.claim: Aḥsan taqwīm is a circumstantial phrase describing the human as formed in the best configuration; taqwīm means shaping and straightening.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r3.claim: He parses the phrase as meaning stature or the one configured, with an implicit genitive; alternatively fī is extra and the phrase is an absolute object.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r4.claim: The best configuration includes upright posture, beauty, sensation, sound intellect, and other outward and inward qualities.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r5.claim: A learned description presents the human as a comprehensive microcosm gathering the seen and unseen and the sources of knowledge and marvels.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r6.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r6.claim: Verses attributed to ʿAlī say a person's cure and illness are within himself and that the greater world is folded into him.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r7.claim: Human qualities such as knowledge, will, and power point toward divine attributes; God also honored humanity by creating Adam with His hands and commanding angels to prostrate.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r8.claim: A report says God created Adam in His image, and in one version in the image of the Merciful; the latter rules out reading the pronoun as mere physical continuity with Adam's descendants.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r9.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p175/r9.claim: He is credited with saying that whoever knows himself knows his Lord; despite popular attribution, it is not established as a prophetic hadith.

ELMALILI:95:4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r1.claim: God created the human species in the best form of bodily and spiritual shaping, ordering, and development; the phrase is a stable adverbial state of the human being.

ELMALILI:95:4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r10.claim: Human beauty is not merely outward form: it lies in feeling and recognizing beauty, knowing God as the absolutely beautiful, and acquiring divine character; this is humanity's intended perfection.

ELMALILI:95:4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r11.claim: Humans are created with the capacity to rise toward this perfection, not born already complete; otherwise no mortality or lowliness would be observable.

ELMALILI:95:4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r12.claim: People begin with burdens and imperfections to shed: some purify themselves and rise, while many lose their share of beauty and sink toward the lowest ranks.

ELMALILI:95:4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r13.speaker: قاضي يحيى بن أكثم، الحنفية
ELMALILI:95:4/r13.claim: A report says Qāḍī Yaḥyā b. Aktham and some Ḥanafīs ruled no divorce occurred when a man conditioned divorce on his wife not being more beautiful than the moon, arguing from this verse.

ELMALILI:95:4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r2.claim: Taqwīm means straightening, ordering, strengthening, or valuing; the indefinite wording intensifies the phrase to encompass every kind of excellence.

ELMALILI:95:4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r3.speaker: النخعي، مجاهد، قتادة
ELMALILI:95:4/r3.claim: Al-Baḥr reports that al-Nakhaʿī, Mujāhid, and Qatāda understand the verse as beauty of human form and senses.

ELMALILI:95:4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r4.claim: Another reported gloss is the straightness of the human stature.

ELMALILI:95:4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r5.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
ELMALILI:95:4/r5.claim: Abū Bakr b. Ṭāhir interprets the best form as adornment with intellect, understanding, and discernment.

ELMALILI:95:4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r6.speaker: عكرمة
ELMALILI:95:4/r6.claim: ʿIkrima understands the best form as youth and strength.

ELMALILI:95:4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r7.speaker: البحر
ELMALILI:95:4/r7.claim: Al-Baḥr's preferred meaning includes every excellence, both bodily beauty and the capacities of intellect and character.

ELMALILI:95:4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r8.claim: Humanity is a comprehensive sign that joins the unseen and visible realms and contains the meanings of the world's wonders and divine secrets.

ELMALILI:95:4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r9.speaker: علي
ELMALILI:95:4/r9.claim: A saying attributed to ʿAlī says that a person's remedy and disease are within, and that the greater world is folded inside the supposedly small human body.

ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.claim: The surah establishes human creation and religion, summarizes the preceding surahs, and prepares for the next; beginning the next surah with Read in your Lord's name is fitting because religion is true and God is the best judge.

QUTB-ZILAL:95:4/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:4/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:4/r1.claim: God initially created the human being in the best form, giving this creature special care and excellence of composition and arrangement.

QUTB-ZILAL:95:4/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:4/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:4/r2.claim: God’s sustained care despite human weakness and deviation shows that people have significance in God’s order, seen in their intricate bodies, distinctive intellect, and remarkable spirit.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.claim: The surah presents Islam as humanity's sound primordial nature and treats departures from its foundations as corruption and misguidance.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r5.claim: The oath's sacred places gesture toward four stages of divine law, suggesting Islam confirms those traditions and shares their foundations.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r6.claim: The surah warns those who reject Islam.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r7.claim: It also reminds people of the favor of being created with an excellent bodily and psychological order.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r1.claim: The oath at places associated with major revealed religions is a fine opening for the surah's claim that humanity was created in sound nature, able to recognize the Creator and His unity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r10.claim: This human distinction lies in harmonizing outward and inward faculties so none corrupts the person or obstructs another faculty's function.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r2.claim: The oath hints that doctrines departing from the foundations of all divine laws have deviated, despite differences in their branches; even this possibility suffices for the opening's rhetorical effect.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r3.claim: The statement that humanity was created in the best constitution, together with what follows, answers the oath.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r4.claim: The constitution and subsequent return are subtle, inward matters requiring reflection, so the oath's emphatic force is apt when most people act as if they deny their natural disposition.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r5.claim: God creates the foundational causes at humanity's beginning and the causes by which descendants develop from them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r6.claim: He links creation to God's statement that He created Adam with His hands and to the creation and shaping of humanity before commanding the angels to bow.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r7.claim: Al-insan may be a generic noun covering all people, or a name for human nature itself regardless of changes affecting individuals, as in the verse “the human was created anxious.”

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r8.claim: The essence reading is like “man is better than woman,” or Imru al-Qays's line that war is initially young, and resembles the use in al-Maʿarij.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p422/r9.claim: Taqwim means placing something in balanced, sound form; the best constitution is the most complete and fitting form for humanity, unlike other creatures.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r1.claim: The preposition fi is figurative for secure possession or attachment; choosing it over a more direct preposition conveys stronger connection concisely.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r2.claim: The verse describes a human constitution fitted to the capacities needed for the species' order and civilization, not physical beauty by itself.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r3.claim: Bodily appearance is not God's criterion for improving the soul, helping others, or reforming the earth; the Prophet says God looks at hearts, not bodies or forms.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r4.claim: Sound perception and reason are God's intended excellence because bodily actions proceed from reason and the body serves it; intellect is humanity's noblest gift.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r5.claim: Reading the best constitution as bodily form and the return as old age does not fit the surah's purpose or warrant its emphatic oath.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r6.claim: The exception for believers shows that faith is the fruit of rational constitution: it guides conduct and good treatment of people who share the truth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r7.claim: This nature may be disrupted before birth by parental disease or injury to the fetus, and after birth by serious illness that distorts temperament.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r8.claim: Long-term intoxicants or drugs can also damage a person's reasoning or weaken resolve and divert the natural constitution.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r1.claim: To fit the old-age interpretation to the surah's aim, one would have to read the lowering as an ungrateful response to a blessing that brings a person low.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r2.claim: As transmitted by Ibn Atiyya from al-Thaʿlabi, Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says the best human constitution consists in intellect and perception adorned with discrimination.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r3.speaker: الأصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r3.claim: Al-Asamm interprets the best constitution as complete intellect, understanding, manners, knowledge, and eloquence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r4.claim: Human nature inclines to benefit and goodness, rejects perceived falsehood or harm, and ordinarily delights in justice, helping the vulnerable, kindness, and honest counsel.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r5.claim: Self-interest, appetite, or anger can temporarily block this disposition; when bad desire wins, people do evil and resist advice in proportion to its control of reason.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p426/r6.claim: Most jurists and hadith scholars therefore hold that people begin in goodness, uprightness, sound judgment, and good intention.

TABATABAI:95:3-6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:95:3-6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:95:3-6/r5.claim: The oath's answer says the human species has the best constitution in every respect; this means humanity is naturally fit to ascend to lasting bliss through useful knowledge and righteous deeds.

TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the bodily-aging reading because it conflicts with the apparently connected exception: creation and aging apply generally to believers and unbelievers alike.

TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.speaker: unnamed view
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.claim: Another view limits the human to the unbeliever and reads the return as casting him into Hell or reversing his bodily form, making the exception disconnected.

ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n2/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n2/r1.claim: The best conformation means physical and mental qualities suited to the functions this creature is meant to perform.

ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n2/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n2/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n2/r2.claim: This relates to the Qur'anic idea that all creation, including the human self, is formed for its intended purpose.

ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n2/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n2/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:1#n2/r3.claim: It does not mean equal bodily or mental endowments: each person can best use their own inborn qualities and environment, whatever their natural advantages or disadvantages.

ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed after surah 85, The Great Constellations.

ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.claim: It states a fundamental moral truth shared by all true religious teachings.

CORPUSCORANICUM:95:4:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:4:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:4:anmerkung/r1.claim: Taqwīm derives from qawwama, meaning to straighten or put into proper condition, and is partly synonymous with creating; the phrase functions adverbially as creating humans in the best manner.

CORPUSCORANICUM:95:4:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:4:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:4:anmerkung/r3.claim: The verse most likely describes each person's formation in the womb, as other Quranic passages use creation language for human development.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.claim: The oaths validate the premise that God created humans in the finest form: those who honor innate guidance, accept the messengers, believe, and do right earn eternal reward, while those who reject it fall into ruin.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r4.claim: Taqwīm literally means straightening something; from this it comes to mean making it fit and suitable for a purpose.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r1.claim: Humans were created for a purposeful trial: resist Satan and his agents, follow God’s straight path, and thereby receive an eternal kingdom; deviation leads to chosen destruction.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r2.claim: The finest mould includes superior bodily form and innate capacities uniquely suited to the trial: moral awareness, love of good, dislike of evil, intellect, and intention.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r1.claim: God swears by four signs of His knowledge, artistry, and power—fig and olive as bodily food, Sinai as revelation's spiritual food, and secure Mecca—to affirm that He made humans best and endowed them to bear physical and spiritual duties (cf. 17:70).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r7.claim: Ahsan taqwim means the finest, most complete human form and structure, making people the most excellent earthly creatures physically, spiritually, and intellectually.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r8.claim: Human excellence reflects God's favors: creating the human with His hand, breathing His spirit (38:72, 38:75), creating in His image, and making humans vicegerents (2:30).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r9.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r9.claim: Commentators see humans as God's most beautiful creatures: living, knowing, willing, speaking, hearing, seeing, reasoning, and governing, they master stronger beings and build cultures; these traits reflect some divine attributes.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r1.claim: God is explicitly the subject of creation because this verse celebrates divine power and artistry; Qur'anic descriptions of bounty similarly assign the action to God.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r2.claim: By contrast, passive creation forms are used when the point is human weakness or defects.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.claim: Al-Inshiqāq begins with human toil and successive ordeals, whereas al-Tīn begins by honoring humanity; its fa therefore suits the emphasis on continuing, unclouded reward.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r3.claim: Naming God as creator also shows that humanity's guide and lawgiver is its creator, who best knows what benefits people; a passive form would not state this clearly.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r6.claim: Best form covers the human being's appearance, meaning, perception, and every material or immaterial excellence.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r7.claim: Thumma marks temporal delay before the low state and a great difference in rank between the best form and the lowest state.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r2.claim: Human development from a drop into a balanced person, through successive stages, proves the creator can resurrect people after death; failure to create them again would be no more difficult than creating them first.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r3.claim: The judgment argument is tightly connected to the preceding account of human creation and decline.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.claim: The oath's answer fits the preceding places of revelation: it describes humanity's beginning in the best form and its eventual return to the lowest state.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.claim: People divide into those who accept the prophetic call and those who refuse it; most are returned low, while believers receive reward.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r32.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r32.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r32.claim: Because revelations provide a way of life for humans, the answer names human nature in verse 4 and the way of life in verse 6; a proper way must suit human nature.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p426/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p426/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p426/r3.claim: God is explicitly the subject of creation because this is a statement of His power, beautiful work, and excellent design; Qur'anic praise and beneficence likewise attribute deeds to Him.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r1.claim: The Qur'an names God as creator when displaying blessing and generosity, but uses passive forms when emphasizing human weakness or flaws.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p427/r2.claim: Naming God as creator identifies Him as the author of humanity's way of life: its Creator alone knows what suits it, a point a passive construction would not state directly.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r1.claim: Aḥsan taqwīm means humanity was fashioned in the best physical and spiritual form, including appearance, meaning, and understanding.

STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.claim: A further view makes the fig the Garden leaves Adam and Eve used to cover themselves and the olive the blessed tree; these may foreshadow human abasement and intellect's light.

STUDYQURAN:95:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r1.claim: The verse answers the oath in vv. 1–3 and affirms humanity's exalted status, reflected in the angels' command to prostrate to Adam.

STUDYQURAN:95:4/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r2.claim: Although made of clay, the human being is proportioned and receives God's Spirit.

STUDYQURAN:95:4/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r3.claim: “Man” means all humanity, female and male, believers and disbelievers.

STUDYQURAN:95:4/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r4.claim: Taqwīm, from qawwama, means raising, shaping, forming, or arranging; here it describes achieving harmonious balance and becoming what one ought to be.

STUDYQURAN:95:4/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r5.claim: One sign of this stature is that humans stand upright while other creatures have faces bent down.

STUDYQURAN:95:4/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r6.claim: Beautiful stature is more than bodily form: the physical symbolizes inner comportment, and humans are God's best creation outwardly and inwardly.

STUDYQURAN:95:4/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r7.claim: A hadith qudsī that God created Adam in His image is understood to mean humans reflect Divine Attributes such as life, knowledge, power, will, speech, hearing, and sight.

STUDYQURAN:95:4/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r8.claim: Humans can manifest all Divine Names and Qualities, unlike other creatures; philosophers call humanity a microcosm containing all created entities.

STUDYQURAN:95:4/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:4/r9.claim: Verses 30:8 and 51:21 call people to reflect on and live according to their exalted status; if vv. 1–3 refer to revelation's locations, stature means receptivity to revelation.

STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.claim: Al-Tīn is likely an early-middle Makkan sūrah revealed after Sūrah 85, though some consider it Madinan; it is named for the fig in verse 1.

STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.claim: Verses 4–6 describe humanity's exalted origin and fall when people fail to live by their true nature, a message like 103:2–3.
